identity.real_world_identity_notes: Stock Car Brasil entry from the Omega era that ran from 1994 to 1999. The 1999 cars kept a heavily modified straight six derived from the 1979 Opala rather than the V8 introduced in 2001, and 1999 was the last season built on production-car chassis. The reviewed source does not document the gearbox, so its five H-pattern gears rest on direct observation rather than a specification.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behavior was directly observed in a guided drive with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.
There is no automation: the clutch is needed to pull away, the driver lifts the throttle to upshift and blips it to downshift.
The gate was observed as a standard H rather than a dogleg, unlike the period European touring cars in this batch.
The registered source does not document the gearbox, so the transmission rests on the guided drive alone.

Knowingly blocked on the downshift blip, recorded rather than carried quietly. The blip is `required` in authentic_controls on the strength of the guided drive, and a drive establishes what AMS2 demands rather than what the real car needed. Where the construction was later established for a car in this position - Formula Vee Gen2, Formula Vee FIN and the Diablo SV-R - the authentic value was revised to optional every time and the simulator's demand moved to an override. Three out of three. So this value is carried without corroboration and is more likely wrong than right; it stays because no source establishes the construction that would settle it, and the dataset does not convert a value by assumption.

What would unblock it: a Stock Car Brasil technical regulation of the period, or constructor documentation. The registered source does not document the gearbox, so the transmission rests on the guided drive alone.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.chevrolet-omega-stock-car-1999.20260813t204024023z-7243ac0f by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behavior was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: Registered sources establish the real-world identity and transmission, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

The source establishes the 1999 Omega Stock Car identity and its straight-six engine but not its transmission. The five gears and H-pattern gate come from the live drive, and the maintainer recorded the gate as a standard H rather than a dogleg.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim. The clutch for a shift already under way follows from gearbox construction, not from the drive.
The guided drive recorded that the upshift was accepted after a throttle lift and the downshift after the driver's manual blip, with no automatic cut or blip detected.

deviations.basis: Gearbox construction is not established for this car, so the running-shift clutch stays unknown rather than inheriting the archetype's dog-box clutchless technique.

The gearbox type is not established. A guided drive cannot separate a synchromesh from a dog box, so unlike the other open fields this one is closed by a reviewed source rather than by driving the car.
Gearbox construction is not established for this car, so the running-shift clutch stays unknown rather than inheriting the archetype's dog-box clutchless technique.

driver_summary: Stock Car Brasil from the Omega era, still on the modified straight six rather than the V8 that arrived in 2001. Five gears and nothing automatic: lift to upshift and blip every downshift. The gearbox construction is not established.
